title: Pan pipes
reference_instrument: an Andean siku, for family likeness and with no count: the nearest isolated tube by pitch from the Wikimedia Commons set Registro sonoro del Siku (D3 from Bajo Sanja - Arca, G3 and D4 from Sanja - Ira, B4 from Contra Suli - Arca; Abel Christian Apaza Amanqui, Sikuri Sumaq Taqi, CC BY-SA 4.0). A siku is a different instrument from the modelled stopped pipes and is not tuned to A440
summary: Nothing here is graded: no licensed pan-pipe recording is in the library, and the clip beside each note is a real siku tube picked by pitch, not the pipe modelled. A twelfth sounds along with each note, even harmonics are far too weak, and the tubes come from published rules, not measurements. Each stopped tube takes its length from its note, its bore from Fletcher's scaling of measured panpipes and its lip-jet controls from flute players' relations, blown one tube at a time. The jet is a forced Bickley jet with momentum drive, Fletcher's 1976 spreading as a trial, a swing limit, a labium offset of half its half-width, and breath noise. About 10 dB of the strong third harmonic sits in the step from the cut flow to the mouth, and which loss is missing is not yet known. D3's fundamental takes about 0.34 s to come within 3 dB of its held level.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a lip jet on one stopped tube at a time, with the blowing pressure and jet length at each pitch from Fletcher 1975's flute-player relations, by analogy, as Fletcher 2005 does for jet speed

The stopped pipe, closed at the far end and open at the blown top, with the tube's length computed from its note and the bore from Fletcher 2005's scaling of European panpipes. The tube's viscothermal wall loss steps its memory exactly, with the flow held over each step (adbb97dbb, f78078db2). The far end is closed and nothing opens it: the card names that closed end as the receiver's outlet, and a closed end's flow is exactly zero, so the clip is the sound of the open top alone. Until 2026-11-07 a vent 2 mm long and 0.1 mm in radius, branching 2 mm below the lip and open to the room, stood in for an outlet; it carried 99 to 100 % of the mean flow entering at the mouth straight out of the tube, which a stopped pipe cannot do, while its own sound was 61 to 66 dB under the mouth's
A forced Bickley jet deflected by the window's own acoustic flow, leaving the flue with a Kutta condition
The jet's momentum drive (Thwaites and Fletcher 1983, Eq. 1, as printed). Without it D3, G3 and D4 sound their third mode, a twelfth above the named note
Jet spreading by Fletcher 1976, a trial here: it was measured on flues of 0.25 to 1.0 mm, and these run from 2.00 mm at D3 to 1.00 mm at B4
A labium offset of half the jet's half-width where it meets the lip (Fletcher 2005, Eq. 6): 1.09, 0.96, 0.80 and 0.62 mm at D3, G3, D4 and B4
A limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, with no coefficient to set. The way it's applied in time is this model's
Contraction loss at the flue exit (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I), carried from the recorder's mouth to a stopped pipe

Breath noise at the window edge (Verge 1995, p. 196): gain 1.3e-3 of the jet's dynamic pressure, from a flue Reynolds number of 700, through an order-two Butterworth band-pass, carried to these flues as an extrapolation
A compact baffled reaction at the mouth, the open top radiating alone, and Stokes-Kirchhoff air along the path to a receiver 1 m above it

The gas Coltman 1968 measured in a played flute's bore (26.15 C, saturated, 2.5 % CO2 dry), applied to a stopped pipe by analogy: a flute is blown across, as this tube is, while the breath pack the whistle and recorder take is for instruments blown into. Dry room air at 20 C outside the tube and along the path to the receiver
physics_missing: A graded comparison: each page sets its note beside one bamboo siku tube, the nearest by pitch among 94 recorded, with no count. A siku is a different instrument and isn't tuned to A440, and the tubes vary widely
A measured instrument: no siku or zampona tube lengths or bores are on the card, so this is a design from published rules

A weaker third harmonic: H3 reads -7.7, -7.1, -6.5 and -6.4 dB re H1 at D3, G3, D4 and B4, where the printed spectra put it at -12 dB near 390 Hz and -28 dB near 760 Hz. Taken apart from the render, about 10 dB of that sits in the step from the cut flow to the flow at the mouth. Neither the jet nor the pipe's resonance height is the cause. One suspect, from reading only: Fletcher describes energy lost to mixing just outside the mouth, and the engine's mouth has no such term

Even harmonics: H2 reads -60.5, -58.5, -55.6 and -51.9 dB at D3, G3, D4 and B4. A stopped pipe takes the second harmonic down 44 to 53 dB on its way to the mouth. Fletcher's two printed notes have about -51 and -28 dB, and the 94 recorded tubes a median of -17.0 dB

A printed jet speed on the low notes: D3 runs at 14.1 m/s and G3 at 16.3 m/s, under Fletcher's stated range of about 20 to 40 m/s. At 20 m/s with the jet length unchanged, on the card before the swing limit, they play the third mode even with the momentum drive. No other jet length was tried

Prompt speech on the low tubes: D3's fundamental takes about 0.34 s to come within 3 dB of its held level, with the tube's third mode above it until about 0.11 s and within 2 dB of it until about 0.24 s
Pitch: the notes read -1.9, -3.1, -6.3 and -11.1 c from equal temperament at D3, G3, D4 and B4. Nothing was aimed at this
Neighbouring tubes aren't coupled, and the array's radiation and the player's lips and face aren't there
The percussive Andean playing style with a turbulent jet. The onset ramp is authored, not a player's

The player's airway (`upstream_airway`, the row the flute's C5, D4 and G4 pages carry, `two-way`, with the voice cards' yielding wall): tried on 2026-11-10 on all four notes, ahead of each tube's lip, with the authored blowing pressure as the lung pressure and nothing rescaled. Each note still plays, lower and quieter on its held part: D3 by 3.2 c and 1.1 dB, G3 by 2.4 c and 0.7 dB, D4 by 1.6 c and 0.4 dB, B4 by 1.0 c and 0.2 dB. D3's fundamental comes within 3 dB of its held level at 0.42 s instead of 0.34 s. Every note already sits flat of the siku tube beside it, so each moved further from it: 21.4 to 24.6 c at D3, 35.7 to 38.2 at G3, 67.0 to 68.6 at D4 and 47.7 to 48.6 at B4. The mean miss of H2 to H12 re H1 against that tube moved 24.4 to 23.5 dB at D3, 20.5 to 19.4 at G3, 15.0 to 15.5 at D4 and 12.0 to 11.9 at B4. That tube is not this pipe, so none of this is a grade; the pages stay without the row
